newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Market selectivity sparks some fire sales.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Market selectivity sparks some fire sales.

text.p: Finicky investors are refusing to buy into initial public offerings without strong prospects and low risks, forcing companies to slash prices for their newly minted shares.

Even deals that had looked hot found themselves with hardly a buyer in sight after a sell-off in technology stocks early last week, analysts said. U.S. Unwired Inc postponed its IPO and Wesley Jessen VisionCare Inc and DAOU Systems Inc and others sharply cut their asking prices.

In sharp contrast to deals that got the cold shoulder, CIENA Corp shares rocketed 40 percent when the maker of telecommunications components made its market debut earlier this month. And other deals have been able to fetch opening day premiums, including Silgan Holdings Inc.
"That kind of divergence is a good sign," said Ryan Jacob, director of research at IPO Value Monitor.
"They are looking at the companies on an individual basis, which is very healthy. It's a very rational market," he said.

Apex PC Solutions, Special Metals Inc, US Unwired Inc and Brylane LP should be the strongest deals coming this week, IPO analysts say, although volume will be slightly lighter due to the shortened holiday week.
U.S. stock markets will be closed on Monday to celebrate Presidents Day.

Apex supplies centralized consoles that manage personal computers that are interconnected in so-called "client/server" networks. Montgomery is the lead underwriter of the offering, which several analysts have said they expect to jump around two points or more at its market debut.

Brylane is a clothing catalog company that retails women's and men's special-size apparel through its Lane Bryant and Roaman's catalogs. It also owns Chadwick's of Boston, which it bought last October from TJX Cos Inc. The company had pro forma net sales of more than $1.1 billion for the latest 12 months.

Merrill Lynch & Co will lead the offering of four million shares with the price estimated at between $24 and $26 a share. John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket, said he expects the deal to rise between 0.75 and one point at its market debut.
He said there is enough demand to push Special Metals up two points ore more and U.S. Rentals by Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette up one to 1.5 points at their market debuts.
